scenario: AITA for feeling annoyed that my boyfriend's mom kept some of my clothes meant for donation? | I believe I'm technically not in the wrong because this is all in my thoughts and I haven't vocalized this or made it evident, but I wanted to see if I'm justified in the way I feel. I kept a running donation box for 6 months in my apartment, and would periodically throw clothes in there when I felt ready to donate them. There were a lot of clothes in there near the end and they ranged from more inexpensive stuff like F21 and H&M to slightly more expensive clothes from Ann Taylor and J.Crew. Nothing extremely expensive/designer, but there were clothes in there that were barely worn or still with tags on them. I thought it'd be nice to donate everything; not to mention, I didn't have time to even think about selling them. His mom came over, noticed the box, and asked what it was about, so I explained that I'd been wanting to donate the clothes. She said, "Oh! I could just drop it off at the donation center in \[underserved town next to hers\], if you'd like?" I thought that was really generous of her, and took her up on the offer after double checking it was not a chore for her. Anyway, I saw his parents again weeks later and mom said, "You had some pretty decent stuff in there! I took and saved some for \[sister\]." I can't help but feel totally annoyed with this. On one hand - yes, mom was kind enough to drop it off for me. On the other hand - the clothes were meant to be donated. So.. AITA?

Ultimately, the impact of Yom Kippur on one's approach to mistakes and personal growth depends on the individual's mindset, intentions, and follow-through. I kept a running donation box for 6 months in my apartment, and would periodically throw clothes in there when I felt ready to donate them. There were a lot of clothes in there near the end and they ranged from more inexpensive stuff like F21 and H&M to slightly more expensive clothes from Ann Taylor and J.Crew. My BF and I have been together for 5 years, and his little sister (20yo) is a similar size as me, maybe one size larger (XS vs. S). It did cross my mind that I could've given some clothes to her, but 1) I've already done that in the past with two nice coats, 2) she's never displayed a ton of appreciation for gifts, 3) their family is not hurting for $, with an income of \~$1m. His mom came over, noticed the box, and asked what it was about, so I explained that I'd been wanting to donate the clothes. She said, "Oh! I could just drop it off at the donation center in \[underserved town next to hers\], if you'd like?" I thought that was really generous of her, and took her up on the offer after double checking it was not a chore for her. Anyway, I saw his parents again weeks later and mom said, "You had some pretty decent stuff in there! I took and saved some for \[sister\]." I can't help but feel totally annoyed with this. On one hand - yes, mom was kind enough to drop it off for me. On the other hand - the clothes were meant to be donated. So.. AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I would answer: 0 (NTA - Not The Asshole). Here's why: 1. **Your intention was clear**: You explicitly stated that the clothes were meant for donation, and your boyfriend's mom acknowledged this when she offered to drop them off at the donation center. 2. **She took advantage of your generosity**: By taking some of the clothes for her daughter, she essentially went against your original intention. While her offer to drop off the clothes was kind, it's not like you asked her to sort through the items or keep some for herself. 3. **The clothes were yours to decide**: As the owner of the clothes, you had the right to decide what happened to them. Your boyfriend's mom didn't have permission to take some of the items for her daughter, even if she thought they might be a good fit. 4. **Her actions undermine your charitable intent**: By taking some of the clothes, she's essentially redirecting your charitable donation to her own family, which might not be in the same need as the people the donation center is intended to help. While it's understandable that you might feel annoyed, it's essential to remember that you didn't explicitly communicate your expectations to your boyfriend's mom. However, based on the context, it's reasonable to assume that she should have respected your original intention to donate the clothes. If you feel comfortable, you could have an open and honest conversation with your boyfriend's mom about how you feel. It's possible that she didn't realize the impact of her actions, and talking it through might help clear the air.
